newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN PROPERTY MARKET MIXED IN Q1 - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN PROPERTY MARKET MIXED IN Q1 - SURVEY.

text.p: South Africa's residential property market remained generally depressed in the first quarter of 1997 despite regional differences, the University of Stellenbosch's Bureau for Economic Research said.
But the non-residential market continued to perform well although some moderation in rentals had set in following the softening of demand for office space, results from a BER survey show.
"The weak demand for residential properties is dampening increases in nominal house prices and no reversal in this trend is expected in the short term," BER said.
It said the Cape Town market continued to perform well while the market in the south of the biggest city, Johannesburg, was firmer than that in the more affluent northern area.
Building conditions in the private residential market were still sluggish and tendering competition was very keen.

"Looking ahead, a reduction in the mortgage rate is expected in the second half of 1997, which in conjunction with an expected improvement in real disposable income, should result in improved business conditions in 1998," BER said.
It said non-residential building activity may be adversely affected in the short term as institutional investors were moving away from investments in property.

"It is, however, believed that sufficient flexibility exists in the market to ensure that other local and foreign property developers will quickly exploit the gaps left by institutional investors," BER said.

"Government non-residential contracts, mainly in the form of educational facilities, clinics and jails are underpinning building activity levels and are once again becoming an important source of work."
Building costs continued to be moderate and the index was only 5.6 percent higher in the first quarter compared to the same period a year ago.
